content:
maya: quick post-run notes from this morning's L2R speculative backoff run on llama3-70b-quant. short summary below, cc @alex @sam

alex: nice. what was the config? schedule?

maya: run config:
```yaml
model: llama3-70b-q
strategy: speculative_l2r_backoff
max_spec_steps: 4
backoff_on_conflict: true
conf_threshold: 0.60
beam: 1
batch_size: 8
cache_policy: warm_prefix_kv
```

maya: results (aggregate over 10k reqs, 512 avg seq):
- p95 latency: 240ms -> 173ms (~28% drop)
- median latency: 120ms -> 95ms (~21% drop)
- tokens/s: +34%
- infra token-cost est: -21%

sam: those numbers look great. any quality regression?

maya: short answer: small regressions on some tasks, details:
- redwood-small-eval (mix of instr, kb, closed QA): perplexity +0.7
- MMLU-style closed-book EM: -1.8% absolute (whole-dataset), concentrated on long-context QA (>1024 tokens)
- instruction-following subjective metrics: slight drop in helpfulness, ~-1.1% (human micro-eval, n=400)
- hallucination-rate (heuristic detect): +1.3% on KB-heavy prompts

maya: failure modes we saw:
- where prefix context had near-duplicates, speculative path picked a shorter continuation leading to truncated answer. example:
```
PROMPT: "Summarize the following thread and list action items."
CONTEXT: repeated user edits (~5 near-duplicates)
SPEC_OUT: incomplete summary, early stop at 2 action items (should be 5)
```
- kv-cache staleness: when warm_prefix_kv wasn't fully populated (cold workers), speculative step used stale KV and then backoff costed extra latency -> some token-level incoherence

liz: can we target fallback only for classes that hurt most? i.e. run rerank fallback when conf < 0.45 and task class in [closed_qa, kb_lookup]?

maya: yes. quick experiment with task-aware fallback (conf_thresh 0.45, class gating) cut the EM regression to -0.6% while preserving ~20% p95 win. small sample though (2k reqs).

alex: what about cost of fallback? if many fallbacks, win evaporates.

maya: we measured that: overall fallback rate 18% under current workload, average fallback added ~40ms on top of speculative path, net p95 still -15% vs baseline. but if fallback >30% the net win disappears.

deploy-bot: canary deployed speculative_l2r_backoff to ded-10 (shard 4) at 2024-07-15T09:12:10Z :rocket:

eval-bench-bot: ran the automated eval suite on the canary. quick links: logs: https://internal.redwood.test/eval/1736543210, artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1736543210/ (full CSV + per-task breakdown).

sam: nice. next experimental steps?

maya: proposal:
- A/B 12h with task-aware fallback (conf 0.55 -> 0.45 sweep) + warm_prefix_kv prefill for 30% of traffic
- log tokens where fallback triggered + full context diffs for 1000 samples
- run per-model (llama3-70b-q, gptx-13b-q) to check transference
- add lightweight reranker (2-step) for top-1 validation on closed-qa

alex: add quantization axis? try int4 vs int8 backend, speculative paths might be more brittle on low-precision kernels.

maya: good call. i'll stitch int4 run overnight and push logs. will tag @liz @sam when ready.

liz: also flagging observability: add counters for speculative_success, fallback_rate_by_task, kv_warm_hit_rate (per worker)

maya: added to checklist. schedule quick sync tomorrow 10:30am PT.

alex: please include the micro-eval prompt set so we can sanity-check instruction regressions.

maya: will attach in the thread when uploaded. short-term goal: keep EM loss <1% and hallucination + <0.8% while retaining >=15% p95 improvement.

sam: ack. thanks for the writeup, Maya. :thumbsup:
